[Question] What happened to Castlevania series? Where did it start its downfall?

I think the downfall started with Symphony of the Night.

There, now that you're done throwing tomatoes at me, let me explain. I love the game. It's really great. It's the reason why we call the style "metroidvania". I think it helped greatly to keep the Castlevania brand relevant until around 2010 where I think it would have otherwise fizzled out around 2000 with the poor N64 version.

The problem with SotN is that it was so beloved that it fractured Castlevania from the classic action platform style to the metroidvania style. Most action platforming games to date had issues getting translated into 3D, so there was a big uphill battle to evolve the classic as the two N64 titles showed, and eventually it would just turn into a hack and slash. It lost it's identity, but at that point it was being kept afloat with the far superior 2d metroidvania titles on handhelds.

Essentially, "Castlevania" stopped being any indicator at all of the type of gameplay and the quality of the experience you will have. Now that even handhelds were shifting hard into primarily 3D experiences in 2011, there's no place for them to live.

Interestingly enough, Metroid did the transition to 3D very well (but was essentially killed by Other M, but we'll see if it makes a come back). Meanwhile the existence of the 2D versions did not have the same fractured experience because they were still basically the same genre of game, just presented differently.
But did presentation, plotlines and other things also contributed to downfall?

A bad plot can still make a good game, so while everything is important, nothing is important, if that makes sense.

Considering Konami is leaving the video games industry, it must have been eyeballing the exit door for quite a while, so it's clear why it wasn't a priority.

Castlevania has never really been a particularly popular franchise. The titles on NES and SNES were pretty good. It kind of disappeared after that. The attempt at making a 3D version was hilariously bad.
Oh, there were questionable design decisions on the NES games as well.

Particularly in the second one. Something about having to crouch in location X with item Y for Z time to advance in the game. It'd be fine and dandy if the game actually told you that, but you were expected to divine this info for yourself.

There were also times where you had to grind before bosses (like Dracula in Castlevania 1) to get a fair chance of beating them. Sometimes the levels didn't complement jump physics of this game either.

I think relying on the Metroid formula without really innovating hurt the series. The inability to move to 3D hurt them too, which meant the series relied on Igarashi for quality 2D games. Then Konami decided to make Igarashi create mobile games instead and handed Castlevania to Kojima. And now Konami has gotten rid of Kojima too. Basically, Konami happened to Castlevania. And for what it's worth, I think the best 3D Castlevania game is Dark Souls.

This article is poorly written with no legal insight at all. The relevant section of the law is Temporary Emergency Gun Violence Restraining Orders, Sec. 18125. The law allows a restraining order to be entered without the knowledge of the individual only if a police officer asserts and a judge finds that there is reasonable cause to believe:

  1. there is an immediate and present danger of causing harm; and
  2. an emergency order is deemed necessary because other options have failed.

Additionally, the temporary order is only in place for 21 days, after which the state must motion for a restraining order, which does require notice to the subject of the order. Temporary Restraining Orders (TRO) for any situation, domestic violence, stalking, etc. all work the same way. No noticed required if the legal test is met, then after 21 days the TRO expire, and the subject of the Restraining Order must be given notice of any attempt at making the TRO last longer than 21 days.

The article is poor journalism used to scare people into believing the government is coming for their guns. Whether you agree with the law or not, it is bad form to characterize it as something it is not.

CHAPTER 2. Temporary Emergency Gun Violence Restraining Order 18125. (a) A temporary emergency gun violence restraining order may be issued on an ex parte basis only if a law enforcement officer asserts, and a judicial officer finds, that there is reasonable cause to believe both of the following: (1) The subject of the petition poses an immediate and present danger of causing personal injury to himself, herself, or another by having in his or her custody or control, owning, purchasing, possessing, or receiving a firearm. (2) A temporary emergency gun violence restraining order is necessary to prevent personal injury to the subject of the petition or another because less restrictive alternatives either have been tried and found to be ineffective, or have been determined to be inadequate or inappropriate for the circumstances of the subject of the petition. (b) A temporary emergency gun violence restraining order issued pursuant to this chapter shall prohibit the subject of the petition from having in his or her custody or control, owning, purchasing, possessing, or receiving, or attempting to purchase or receive, a firearm or ammunition, and shall expire 21 days from the date the order is issued.
